comparator.name: Dutch Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The current annual catalogue verifies 60 EC in year one and identifies 55 distinct EC for year two. The year-two list repeats the first-year 5 EC Humanities in a Digital World course. The previous annual guide and the transitional table do not confirm a distinct replacement for September 2026 entrants. Current year-three course records identify 10 EC Academic Reading and Writing in semester one, the 10 EC thesis and zero-credit seminar in semester two, and split 15 EC elective placeholders. The concentration parent gives 15 EC while its two branches each specify 10 EC and programme prose describes two advanced courses. Thesis and seminar normally follow the first two years and advanced academic writing. Earlier programme wording about an open first semester does not establish the current entrant timetable.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Dutch Studies degree is designed for non-native speakers of Dutch. Students develop Dutch language skills and study the literature, history, art and society of the Netherlands. The programme culminates in a thesis in Dutch.
